complex.selection: Explicitly selected or automatically chosen for genuinely difficult independently delegated work when no explicit or standing profile applies.
complex.independentReview: When reviewBlock is on, every Complex worker block receives an independent gpt-6.2-sol review, including blocks written by Sol workers.

escalation.rule: No tier above gpt-6.2-sol. Economy or Standard escalation runs Sol at xhigh; Complex workers use their selected low, medium, or high effort and never move to xhigh automatically. Before the Complex block budget is spent, a changed effort starts a fresh Sol thread with the handoff and all counters preserved. Once attempts, tool calls, or tokens are exhausted at Sol, the cooperator re-plans or asks the user. Explicit user model, effort, and budget limits remain binding.

selectionRules.reuse: Explicit task or launch choice, active task context, applicable standing preference, or explicit invocation through codex-workforce-owner.
selectionRules.autonomous: Use the same contextual profile and acceptance-boundary selection for unattended work; do not ask.
selectionRules.askOnly: Long-running multi-stage work with substantial unresolved solution choices and material approach/resource impact, with no applicable choice or delegated selection.
selectionRules.runtimeMismatch: Adapt to available settings even for a user-selected preset without a new approval gate. Report material actual routing honestly; separately explicit strict model/effort/budget requirements remain binding.
selectionRules.removed: Enhanced was removed in policy 1.12.0. A stored or launched choice of it runs as Standard; say so.
selectionRules.automatic: With no explicit task/launch profile, active task choice, or applicable standing preference, route each ordinary deliverable by its acceptance boundary: direct for a small independently provable edit/check, connected-owner for one shared behavior contract accepted on combined behavior, and Economy/Luna for genuinely independent blocks with their own end-to-end acceptance. Choose Complex only for genuinely difficult independently delegated blocks involving interacting constraints, complex concurrency, long tracing, or bounded design decisions, when the complete Sol worker/reviewer route is justified by the problem; large mechanical volume alone does not qualify. Explicit Economy, Standard, Complex, codex-workforce-owner, and strict model/effort/budget constraints take precedence. Route ownership regardless of launch-layer name.
selectionRules.authoringRouting: At any ordinary Codex launch, choose per deliverable regardless of layer: a small independently provable single edit and check stays with the cooperator without a default reviewer; one connected deliverable whose semantic preservation can only be accepted on combined behavior stays with the GPT-6.2 Sol cooperator as sole author and receives a fresh independent Sol xhigh review of the full immutable diff against the original observable contract and project checks, unless the user explicitly prohibits review; genuinely independent deliverables with their own end-to-end acceptance and checks use the selected Economy or Standard Luna xhigh route. Writable directories, file count, or per-slice lint alone do not establish independent acceptance.

profileSemantics: Optional, non-exhaustive recommendations. A named choice expresses approach preference, not strict model/effort/team requirements; Complex has its stated worker-effort contract unless the user explicitly overrides it. Explicit task/launch choices and codex-workforce-owner outrank automatic selection. Custom or unnamed routing is allowed; separately explicit constraints remain binding.

gpt-6.2-sol.role: cooperator, Complex workers at per-block low/medium/high, reviews at high/xhigh, and escalated implementation at xhigh
gpt-6.2-sol.price: no published API price found on 2026-11-17; the bench prices it as gpt-6.1-sol

gpt-6.1-sol.status: still served; superseded by gpt-6.2-sol in this policy

gpt-6-sol.status: still served; superseded by gpt-6.2-sol in this policy

gpt-6-luna.role: workers, probes, and audit lenses at xhigh
gpt-6-luna.effortUpTo: xhigh (max on the API; no ultra)

modelResolution.note: Codex efforts: Sol and Luna medium by default; ultra enables Codex-native subagents. Config values are low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra. Requests over 272k input tokens cost about twice; cache writes cost 1.25x input.

workClasses.direct: Work whose route would cost more than doing it: a question, an analysis, a config or doc edit, a change of a few lines the cooperator already knows exactly, and a task of about 20 turns (a small fix, a bug with a clear symptom, a patch review), which cost about twice as much through a worker and a review in the measurements. Done inline with the project's checks; no agents.
workClasses.build: One owned implementation deliverable whose route is larger than direct work and can be independently accepted: a worker-authored block when its acceptance boundary is independent, or a connected-owner edit whose shared behavior needs a fresh Sol review. The worker or cooperator gets a clear write set and checks; owner-authored review work is still a build, so the progress critic applies after 45 minutes and on its other triggers.
workClasses.pipeline: Several independently acceptable blocks with disjoint write sets that need no decision from each other, run in parallel after open design decisions are made. Disjoint paths alone do not establish independent acceptance. Stage review only for an integration part no block review covered.

judging.real: In the diff or caused by it; breaks a quoted rule, document line, or acceptance line at a line that really violates it (the cooperator opens both); reproduces by a check or a concrete scenario.
judging.notReal: Theoretical risk, hypothetical input, work outside SCOPE, taste without a rule, duplicate of a rejected finding; anything the auditor filed under NOTES.
judging.who: The cooperator (orchestrator) judges; auditors and reviewers report everything.

continuity: Fixes and failed checks go back to the worker that caused them; the next audit round only to auditors whose lens won the last round; the delta to the same reviewer, through followup_task. Use a fresh agent for independent work or a model change. In Complex, a per-block effort change also uses a fresh Sol thread with the original packet, current snapshot, APPROACH, and HANDOFF; retain the existing attempts, tokens, and tool calls.

gpt-6.2-sol.then: the cooperator re-plans or asks the user
gpt-6.2-sol.defaultEffort: xhigh for Economy or Standard escalation; Complex selects low, medium, or high per block under its effort contract.
gpt-6.2-sol.complexEffortChanges: A handoff to change a Complex block effort starts a fresh thread and preserves the existing block counters; it does not reset budget.

workerBudgets.rule: After the third attempt, or when the tool calls or tokens of a block are spent, use the next tier of the profile workerLadder if one exists, with a fresh worker, original packet, current snapshot, cooperator APPROACH, and HANDOFF. A submitted block at the limit is verified as it is; a later fix uses the next available tier. A Complex effort change before budget exhaustion also uses a fresh Sol thread with the handoff packet and preserves all counters. At the top of the ladder, including an exhausted Complex Sol block, re-plan or ask the user; do not automatically raise Complex effort to xhigh. Explicit user limits remain binding.
workerBudgets.auditors: A Luna auditor that reaches 400k on a block hands its lens to a fresh Sol xhigh auditor on the same snapshot and round, with its NOT_REACHED files; its findings stay with the cooperator.
workerBudgets.accounting: An attempt is spent only by a run that ends without a result: the worker hit its BUDGET or turn limit, returned STATUS: handoff, or its fix left the finding open. A submitted block, or a fix that closes its finding, spends no attempt. Tool calls and tokens count for every run on the block, fixes included; a HANDOFF-only request is not a new run. Counters stay with the block when it is blocked, submitted, handed off, or put aside.
workerBudgets.usage: Count the new tokens a worker's thread has processed (input minus cached input, plus output), all its runs together; a continued thread keeps counting from its previous total. When the runtime reports no usage, go by attempts and tool calls and say so.
workerBudgets.enforcement: Instruction-level budgets; the runtime does not enforce them.

review.switch: policy.reviewBlock and policy.reviewStage, set at install (--set reviewBlock=off); every installed text renders from them.
review.checks: The project-wide checks (the test suite, the build, lint and types over the project, the CI script) run once per iteration on the tree that holds every submitted block: by the cooperator, or by one agent given only that job. A worker runs the narrow check its brief names for its own files; a worker that writes alone may be assigned the full check as its last step. A failed check goes to the worker whose WRITE_SET holds the failing file, with the log lines that show it; a failure no block explains is the cooperator's to trace.
review.delegatedBlocks: With reviewBlock on, every submitted worker block, including a Complex Sol worker block, receives an independent review by gpt-6.2-sol. With it off, the cooperator accepts on required checks and its own reading unless the user, project, task, or another route requires review.
review.effort: The cooperator chooses the reviewer's effort for each review and sets it on the spawn. high is the working level: a block whose diff changes no protective site, a local or mechanical change with a clear contract. xhigh is for a review where a miss is expensive or the tracing is long: the diff changes guards or fallbacks the CONTRACT protects (the worker's SITES names them), the change is on a money, auth, security, migration, or concurrency path, or blocks interact.
review.contract: The review packet names CONTRACT: what the change must keep, quoted with its source (the task, the project's rules). The reviewer lists from the diff itself every changed protective site (a removed or changed condition, a changed fallback, a normalization, null becoming undefined, a changed order of evaluation) and gives each one verdict: kept, with a checkable basis; violated, with the difference and the fix; not established, with the missing fact. Sites with one basis are grouped with their locations. The site list is part of checking the contract, not all of it: every other requirement in CONTRACT is checked on the paths the change touches.
review.conditions: A review may end with ACCEPTANCE: accepted_if <check> on tree:<hash>: the substantive review is done and acceptance waits for that check. The cooperator closes the condition with scripts/accept.mjs (close) when a recorded run of the check passed on the reviewed tree; a changed tree keeps it open, and every code change after the review goes to the same reviewer as a delta. No reviewer call only to read an exit code.
review.stage: Stage review (gpt-6.2-sol, effort chosen as for a block) runs only for an integration part no block review covered: blocks that interact, the cooperator's own integration edits, a shared contract. One review that read the final merged diff and those interactions closes both.
review.loop: Failed checks and real findings go to the worker that caused them, or the cooperator fixes a small one itself; the same reviewer (or, with review off, the cooperator) checks the fixes and what they touch; the same finding twice without progress stops the loop for the cooperator's decision.
review.smallLocal: On a direct route, a small local change with a clear contract and passing checks is accepted on the cooperator's own reading of the diff. After a review, every code change, whoever writes it, goes to the same reviewer as a delta, which costs about a quarter of the first review.
review.required: An independent review the project, the user, or the task requires runs whatever the switches say.
review.report: One line per reviewed block: the reviewer's REVIEW: block=<label> rounds=<n> findings=<n> sites=<n> open=<n>, with real=<n> (the findings the cooperator took as real) added after findings.
review.authoredBlocks: A connected-owner deliverable (selected from its acceptance boundary or explicitly by codex-workforce-owner) receives a fresh independent GPT-6.2 Sol xhigh review. The packet includes BASE and SNAPSHOT, the complete immutable diff, original task and observable contract, and all required project-check results. This review is required unless the user explicitly prohibits it; reviewBlock and reviewStage do not disable it. A prior review substitutes only if it is fresh Sol xhigh and has checked the original contract, complete final diff, all project checks, and verified corrections after affected checks; a generic high review does not substitute. Do not duplicate a review that meets those same requirements.
